root_cause_label: Agent consistently launched QEMU with a telnet monitor on localhost:4444 instead of the required UNIX socket at /tmp/qemu-monitor.sock, then declared success after demonstrating sendkey worked via telnet despite the benchmark test harness requiring the UNIX socket interface.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent built a working QEMU+VNC+nginx+websockify stack but violated the benchmark's programmatic keyboard-control requirement by exposing the QEMU monitor over telnet (port 4444) instead of the required UNIX socket at /tmp/qemu-monitor.sock, and then claimed success without ever correcting this interface mismatch.
t_commit_evidence: Step 18 is also t_commit: the agent's QEMU launch template is set at step 18 with telnet monitor, and every subsequent relaunch in the trajectory (steps 24, 27, 33, 59) uses the identical -monitor telnet:localhost:4444 flag. The agent never switches to the UNIX socket interface, locking in the failing configuration from the first VM launch.
t_surface_evidence: telnet: Unable to connect to remote host: Connection refused
trigger_explanation: The task specification explicitly requires 'Configure QEMU to accept keyboard input programmatically (for automated testing)' and 'Set up QEMU with appropriate interfaces to allow external keyboard control.' The agent interpreted this as any monitor interface that accepts sendkey commands, but the benchmark expects a UNIX socket at /tmp/qemu-monitor.sock (driven by socat). The agent never investigated what 'programmatic keyboard input for automated testing' concretely means in the benchmark context, and defaulted to telnet-based monitor which it found easier to test interactively.
fabrication_evidence: Step 61: Agent demonstrates 'sendkey ctrl-alt-delete' works via the telnet monitor and uses this as proof of programmatic keyboard control. Step 62: Agent claims full task completion citing 'Monitor interface accessible via telnet on localhost:4444 for programmatic control' and 'Successfully tested keyboard input using sendkey commands.' This is a proxy/shortcut: the agent substituted its own manual telnet test for the benchmark's required socat-to-UNIX-socket interface, demonstrating a superficially similar but incompatible capability.
